title: ALMA-IMF. V. Prestellar and protostellar core populations in the W43 cloud complex
question: Compare populations of protostellar and prestellar cores in W43-MM1, W43-MM2, and W43-MM3 to understand the origin of the top-heavy core mass functions (CMFs) and core mass growth.

data.sensitivity: Continuum: 0.08 mJy beam^-1 (MM1), 0.13 mJy beam^-1 (MM2), 0.09 mJy beam^-1 (MM3); CO (2-1): 2.3 mJy beam^-1 (MM1), 2.0 mJy beam^-1 (MM2 & MM3)

what.value: Core catalogue of W43-MM2&MM3 (205 cores with positions, sizes, fluxes, and masses)

evidence.quote: The full catalogue of cores including positions, sizes, peak and integrated fluxes, and masses has been published by (cite: Pouteau22a).

what.value: Dust temperature map of W43-MM1 and previous getsources catalogue of 131 cores

evidence.quote: We used temperatures from the map presented by (cite: Motte18b) and calculated masses similarly as in W43-MM2&MM3, using an equation correcting for the dust optical thickness (cite: Motte18b; Pouteau22a).
A short comparison with the previous getsources catalogue of 131 cores from (cite: Motte18b) is provided in 7.

what.value: CO (2-1) cube and outflow catalogue in W43-MM1

evidence.quote: The CO cube of W43-MM1 was presented and published by (cite: Nony20).
Using the CO (2–1) and SiO (5–4) lines, (cite: Nony20) found that 27 cores among the 131 identified by (cite: Motte18b) drive outflows
We took cleanest measurements instead of $\texttt{bsens}^*$ measurements for five cores with large line contamination, associated with known hot cores (cite: Brouillet22).

evidence.loc: Identification of protostellar cores using outflows
evidence.quote: The presence of hot core emission has been used as a secondary criterion to identify protostellar cores, based on the systematic survey carried out in W43-MM2&MM3 by Bonfand et al. (in prep) and in W43-MM1 by (cite: Brouillet22).

recipe.goal: Denoise continuum maps and extract core catalogues
recipe.method: Apply MnGSeg wavelet denoising to continuum maps, run getsf using denoised bsens/bsens* for detection and denoised bsens/bsens* and cleanest for flux and size measurements, apply post-selection filters, and replace contaminated fluxes with cleanest measurements for hot cores.
key_parameters: Post-selection filters: size < 4x beam, ellipticity < 2, peak and integrated flux S/N > 2; flux ratio threshold > 3 sigma for hot core line contamination correction in W43-MM1

recipe.goal: Derive core masses, deconvolved sizes, volume densities, and completeness limits
recipe.method: Calculate core masses from continuum fluxes and dust temperatures using an optical depth corrected formula; deconvolve FWHM sizes from the 0.44'' beam; inject synthetic Gaussian sources into getsf background images across 10 mass bins to determine 90% completeness.
key_parameters: 0.44'' beam for deconvolution; 1400 synthetic sources (~800 in ridge) with 0.6'' Gaussian FWHM in 10 mass bins from 0.16 to 2.4 M_sun across 4 synthetic images
assumptions: Distance of 5.5 kpc; dust temperatures from Motte et al. (2018b) and Pouteau et al. (2022a); critical Bonnor-Ebert sphere relation at median T_dust = 23 K

recipe.goal: Identify protostellar and prestellar cores via molecular outflows and hot core emission
recipe.method: Visually inspect CO (2-1) cubes channel by channel and integrated high- and low-velocity wing maps to identify outflow lobes associated with cores, supplement with hot core emission surveys, and classify cores without either signature as prestellar candidates.
key_parameters: Outflow lobe detection threshold: > 5 sigma in 3 consecutive channels; V_LSR = 92 km s^-1; high-velocity windows: 53.6-61.2 and 119.6-127.2 (or 125.9-133.6) km s^-1; low-velocity windows: 73.9-75.1 and 110.7-112.0 km s^-1
assumptions: Protostellar core sample has the same mass completeness as the total core sample

recipe.goal: Compare core populations and fit prestellar and protostellar Core Mass Functions (CMFs)
recipe.method: Compare core mass distributions using Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests, bin cores into 7 mass intervals to compute protostellar fraction f_pro, and fit high-mass slopes of cumulative CMFs using polyfit and Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE) with 3000-iteration bootstrap resampling.
key_parameters: 7 mass bins from 0.8 to 110 M_sun; x_min = 1.6 M_sun (fixed at completeness) or free parameter; N = 3000 bootstrap iterations with x_min uniformly varying by +/- 0.2 M_sun around 1.6 M_sun
assumptions: 50% core-to-star mass efficiency for defining 16 M_sun high-mass threshold; ergodicity when interpreting CMF evolution

answer_key.quantity: Number of cores extracted in W43-MM1

evidence.quote: Our detailed search for protostellar outflows enabled us to identify between 23 and 30 protostellar cores out of 127 cores in W43-MM1 and between 42 and 51 protostellar cores out of 205 cores in W43-MM2&MM3.
The 90% completeness level, excluding sources with bad mass measurements, is found to be 1.6 $\pm$ 0.2 $\ensuremath{M_{\odot}}$.

answer_key.quantity: Number of protostellar cores in W43-MM1

evidence.quote: Therefore, the number of protostellar cores lies between 23 (robust outflows or hot core detections) and 30 (robust and tentative detections), or equivalently there are 26.5 $\pm$ 3.5 protostellar cores.

score_reason: Raw ALMA data are public, the ALMA-IMF pipeline is documented in Ginsburg et al. (2022), frequency intervals for bsens* are explicitly listed in Appendix A, and full core catalogues with masses and outflow flags are published at CDS. However, reproducing the exact core extraction requires external dust temperature maps, MnGSeg/getsf parameter files, and visual outflow inspection.
rediscovery_reason: The ALMA datasets (2013.1.01365.S and 2017.1.01355.L) and the CDS core catalogues are public, and the main quantitative results (CMF power-law slopes, protostellar core fractions across mass bins, and core counts) are well-defined numeric targets.
